title: Definition clash: Roman firm assent vs Reformed fiducia definitions
source_text: LII. Jam autem in definienda fide justificante multum dissentire videntur a Reformatis Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae. Nam hi quidem fidem unanimi consensu definiunt firmum assensum adhibitum omnibus iis quae sunt Verbo Dei revelata propter Dei revelantis authoritatem & testimonium: Reformati vero varias, & quae multum diversae videntur, fidei justificantis definitiones tradunt. Et quidem nonnulli sunt qui jam allatam fidei definitionem probant & usurpant, nisi quod addunt fidem salvificam assensum esse efficacem, & qui potissimum circa promissiones gratiae versetur. Alii vero plerique fidem definiunt, certam fiduciam qua nobis Christi meritum applicamus, aut salutis per Christum obtinendae certam fiduciam & apprehensionem. Vel etiam, ut ante latius expositum fuit, acquiescentiam cordis in Deo, tanquam in authore vitae & salutis aeternae, ut per ipsam ab omni malo liberemur, & omne bonum consequamur, & quae sunt in hunc aut similem sensum.
pass_a_gloss: Now in defining justifying faith the Doctors of the Roman Church seem to dissent much from the Reformed. For these indeed by unanimous consent define faith as a firm assent given to all things revealed by God Word on account of the authority and testimony of God revealing; but the Reformed hand down various definitions of justifying faith that seem much diverse. And indeed there are some who approve and use the definition of faith already brought forward, except that they add that saving faith is an efficacious assent and one that especially turns about the promises of grace. But most others define faith as a certain trust by which we apply Christ merit to ourselves, or a certain trust and apprehension of salvation to be obtained through Christ. Or also, as was set out more fully before, a resting of the heart in God as in the author of life and eternal salvation, that through it we may be freed from every evil and obtain every good, and things in this or a similar sense.
pass_b_english: Rome unanimously defines faith as firm assent to all God has revealed because of the Revealer authority; Reformed definitions of justifying faith look more varied.
Some Reformed keep assent but add efficacy and focus on grace-promises; most define by fiducia applying Christ merit, or heart-rest in God as author of eternal life.

lemmas.gloss: a resting of the heart in God

choices.why: Rome absolute definition vs Reformed fiducia-heavy defining.
